prompt:
Generate one high-quality cinematic 16:9 image for the specified section, not a generic slide or dashboard. No letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, arrows, diagrams, interface, checkmarks, traffic-light statuses or readable documents. The compositor adds every semantic mark independently. Do not invent a completed publication, a live security test, a solved outing, approval or consensus. Fictional editorial staging, not documentary evidence. Rich material detail, carefully controlled light, credible objects and hands. Keep designated annotation zones visually quiet. Never fill quiet zones with invented panels. Reference images establish cast and room identity only; follow this section's camera and blocking.
VISUAL FORMAT: identity-mismatch-macro
TEACHING PURPOSE: Show why a grant for one object cannot authorize another.
CAMERA: Extreme close-up of two incompatible physical fittings.
Editorial macro photograph of two elegant unmarked machined-metal fittings that almost meet but visibly do not align, one matte silver at LOWER LEFT and one dark copper at LOWER RIGHT. Clear gap between them. Dark blue studio background, shallow depth, crisp controlled side light. Entire UPPER HALF is quiet near-black for large identity typography. No keys with labels, no circuit, no arrows, no lock-opening action. This is a visual metaphor for mismatch, not a claim about physical security.
COMPOSITING INTENT: The grant's C-17 and request's C-18 sit on opposite sides of a visible gap; one changed character is emphasized, with HOLD centered in the gap.
SEMANTIC AUTHORITY FOR CONTEXT ONLY, NEVER RENDER THESE WORDS: LOCAL TOY SIMULATION. Change the object to C eighteen, keeping the old grant. The dispatcher holds the request: the object no longer matches. Changing approved arguments must also invalidate the match. Permission belongs to the bound action, object, and arguments, not to a reassuring label.
